newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RALLYING-MAKINEN REIGNS SUPREME IN ARGENTINA.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MAKINEN REIGNS SUPREME IN ARGENTINA.

text.p: Reigning world rally champion Tommi Makinen clinched his third victory of the season by winning the Rally of Argentina for the second year in a row on Saturday.
The Finn extended his lead at the head of the world rally drivers' standings, finishing one minute one second clear of second-placed Colin McRae with Swede Kenneth Eriksson third.
The Mitsubishi driver never looked like losing the lead after beginning the final day with a comfortable advantage over second-placed British rival Colin McRae.
On the day's first stage, McRae was fastest but only managed to reduce the gap by two seconds and when the 20th stage, the day's second, was cancelled overhauling Makinen proved too much.

The rally is reported to have attracted 250,000 spectators a day and the stage was cancelled for safety reasons when tens of thousands of the enthusiastic followers wandered too far on to the rallying track road.
The next stage brought the retirement of Spaniard Carlos Sainz. The Ford driver, the only other championship contender to Makinen and McRae, stopped with an overheated engine.
Makinen won on the gravel surface at Portugal earlier this year and again proved that he and the Mitsubishi car were the perfect combination on the similar Argentine course.
As the field headed back to the start at Cordoba, he emphasised his dominance on the penultimate stage from Amboy to Rosa Calamuchita when he finished fastest, nine seconds ahead of McRae.
McRae, who crashed out chasing Makinen in similar circumstances last year, admitted he was content with second place.
He said: "We had little chance of catching Tommi and it would have been silly to throw away our position trying to do so. I cannot blame the stage cancellation as it had little affect on the result.
"We have got six points and it is not what we came here for but it is best to come away with at least something."

McRae is now looking forward to the remaining seven rounds. "We are now halfway through the season and I am only six points behind Tommi. Also with the exception of San Remo the rallies in the second half of the season suit me."
The Argentinian Rally leaves Makinen with 38 points in the world championship, six points ahead of McRae, with Sainz third on 18.
Subaru are in a dominating position in the manufacturers' table. They have 64 points, 18 points ahead of Mitsubishi, with Ford on 29.
